Data & Platforms: University of Oklahoma Health Sciences Center (OUHSC) dataset
Application Areas: Medical Image Segmentation and Anomaly Detection
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Weakly Supervised Generative Segmentation: Utilizing Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) with classifier guidance to translate diseased medical images into healthy counterparts, enabling precise pancreatic tumor segmentation using only image-level labels without pixel-level masks.

Cryptographic Integrity Verification: Integrating Zero-Knowledge Proofs (ZKP) with polynomial proxy models (ProxyZKP) to ensure computation integrity in decentralized federated learning, achieving faster proof generation than zk-SNARKs while mitigating gradient inversion attacks via differential privacy.

Information-Theoretic Routing Optimization: Enhancing Capsule Network robustness and interpretability by introducing Entropy Adjusted Dynamic Routing (EADR), which applies information-theoretic entropy regularization to reduce reliance on uncertain part-whole connections during vector-valued unit routing.

Comparative Forensic Analysis: Systematically evaluating the arms race between generative AI (GANs, Diffusion Models) and detection methodologies, identifying critical gaps in real-time performance and cross-modal detection capabilities to inform robust media security frameworks.
Summary Description: Samuel Cheng specializes in the intersection of medical image analysis, secure distributed computing, and media forensics. His research leverages advanced deep learning architectures, particularly Denoising Diffusion Models and Capsule Networks, to solve complex problems in weakly supervised medical segmentation and robust object recognition. Concurrently, he addresses critical security challenges in AI by developing privacy-preserving frameworks that integrate Zero-Knowledge Proofs with federated learning to ensure data integrity and prevent gradient inversion attacks. His work also critically examines the evolution of deepfake technologies, providing systematic insights into the limitations of current detection methods against state-of-the-art generative models. Cheng’s contributions bridge the gap between high-performance algorithmic design and rigorous security/privacy guarantees in critical applications like healthcare and digital media integrity.
